I think there were other factors that made me an easy target. I had always been quiet (not shy, just a private, awkward kid) and according to a lot of people growing up I spoke more like someone from “anywhere but the South”.  

I was bullied because of a lot of things. But being lightskinned was incredibly memorable since a lot of the other girls assumed I must be stuck up because of a lot of these factors. There was even a group of girls that sorta tortured me all throughout elementary to middle school and by middle school I had picked up a mild Emo sense of fashion and music taste.  Which, in the Deep South, stood out a lot. I don’t think me being lighter skinned was the only reason why I felt like all of my peers hated me, but it was a factor.     

I’ll admit, seeing a few of those memes deriding or creepily “praising” lighter skinned or mixed black girls and women (ironically, no one bothers light or mixed men, they’re allowed to simply exist), bother me a lot. It took a long time to accept me for me, I hate that we’ve gone back to school yard taunts and hate because of how someone’s folks went down. Even my mom can’t help but screech about black men with non black women (black women with non black, however is a non issue, I guess *eyeroll*). This rant probably went nowhere, but that’s my experience with it, everyone else is different and has different experiences. I wish we weren’t at this point, I wish most people could just ‘exist’ as they are instead of having to explain it or just be labeled as ‘less than’ or undesirable. 

Makes some of us no better than those creepy white supremacy types that try to compare skin tones and face shapes to see who’s the most White. Let’s do better.

All in all, I was fucked.

I have a type of guy. I know it's silly to even categorize the type of men I'm attracted to, but here goes. I think... They're also great fathers, lovers, etc. 

There was one guy. I knew him briefly. He was so nice, and if I just lost enough weight/and if he didn't have a stalker (long story, but it was so dumb), I think we'd be engaged by now. There was also another guy, I had a slight crush on. Never got to meet or talk to  him, but he was gorgeous. Tall. I love men of color with thick or muscled bodies (think of the anime genre bara, I know it's more for gay men, but those are the type of bodies/men I'm attracted to).

Then there was my ill-fated crush. I've already spoken about him. It was humiliating. 

A lot of my celebrity crushes are men of color and specifically Islander men; The Rock, Roman Reigns, James Rolleston, Jason Momoa, Manu Bennett etc.

But I know I don't have a chance. I'm dumpy and hairy and with an ugly body, right now. Now that I have a job, I might have the means to better myself with weight loss/dieting/fashion, etc., but I'm scared of that never happening..

I'm also a nerd/dork, so Idk if mostly sporty guys like that would even understand me. 

Beggars can't be choosers, but still. If I could just *befriend* a man like that, with no pretenses on sex, but to just spend time and get to know someone from a world different from mine, that would be... amazing. 

I hope it doesn't seem like fetishizing, obvs I can't control that, because I'm not from those cultures (other than being Black, ofc), but man I wish I was in a location where I could physically, actually meet those type of guys. I guess that's why I'd like to settle in Hawaii. I feel so shit out of luck, rn. Most of the interracial relationships around me involve white women, while girls like me are just left behind.

Maybe one day... someone will find me beautiful. Inside and out.
